chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from a man who asked al-Rida عليه السلام about prayer in

fox skins, so he forbade prayer in them and in the garment that is next to them. He did not know which of the two garments was the one that sticks to the fur or the one that sticks to the skin, so he wrote in his own hand: the garment that sticks to the skin. And Abu al-Hasan mentioned that he asked him about this issue, and he said: Do not pray in the one above it, nor in the one beneath it.

key_terms.الثَّوْبِ: garment or cloth worn by a person
key_terms.الْوَبَرِ: fur or soft hair on the animal skin

ai.seo_question: Can one perform salat while wearing garments made from or attached to fox skins?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning salat in garments associated with fox skins. It indicates prohibition not only of praying in the skin itself, but also in garments directly connected with it, clarifying the practical application of the ruling.
